sections.h2: Where is Moniteau County and what is its housing market like?
sections.html:
Moniteau County sits in central Missouri and belongs to the Jefferson City metropolitan area. California is the county seat and largest city. The county was organized on February 14, 1845, and takes its name from Moniteau Creek. It covers about 419 square miles, 415 of them land, and borders Cooper, Boone, Cole, Miller and Morgan counties. U.S. Route 50 and Missouri Routes 5, 87 and 179 are its main highways.

The Census Bureau estimated 15,428 residents in July 2025, close to the 15,473 counted in 2020. Its QuickFacts page shows 6,189 housing units, a 79.2 percent owner-occupied rate and a median owner-occupied home value of $181,900 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent was $735 and median household income was $65,715. Only 6 building permits were recorded for 2025. The 2020 census counted every resident as living in a rural area.

Towns include California, Clarksburg, Jamestown, Lupus and Tipton, with Fortuna and Latham as census-designated places. Public schools run through six districts: Clarksburg C-2, High Point R-III, Jamestown C-1, Moniteau County R-I in California, Moniteau County R-V in Latham and Tipton R-VI.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Moniteau County?
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices share the work, both at 200 E. Main Street in California. The assessor values property and the collector bills and collects.

  • Assessor. Room 105, phone 573-796-4637, email assessor@moniteaucountymo.gov. The assessor's site says the office values all tangible real and personal property in the county and keeps an open door policy. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays.
  • Collector. Room 101, phone 573-796-4521. The collector's site says the office prepares real estate and personal property statements, collects the tax, distributes funds monthly to the taxing entities, issues merchant licenses and runs the delinquent tax sale in August. It is open the same hours and stays open through lunch.
  • Recorder. The circuit clerk also serves as recorder, in Room 102, phone 573-796-2071, according to the Missouri Association of Counties.

The collector's office suggests checking each statement for the right mailing address, vehicles and legal description. Payments can be made in person, by phone, by mail or online, using cash, personal check, e-check, money order or credit card.

sections.h2: How is a Moniteau County house assessed?
sections.html:
The assessor values real property in odd-numbered years, and those values carry into the following even-numbered year. Under section 137.115, new values are set as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year, and new construction and improvements are valued as though finished on that January 1. Because 2026 is an even year, bills now arriving generally reflect the values set as of January 1, 2025, and the next general reassessment date is January 1, 2027.

The same statute sets assessment percentages: real property in subclass 1 is assessed at 19 percent of true value, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent. Personal property is assessed at 33 and one third percent, with lower rates for items such as livestock and farm machinery. Ask the assessor which subclass your parcel is in. Manufactured homes used as dwellings are assessed at the same percentage as residential real property.

Before the assessor raises a subclass 1 parcel's value by more than fifteen percent over its last assessment, not counting new construction, the assessor must physically inspect it. The owner can ask for an interior inspection and has at least thirty days to make that request after written notice.

sections.h2: When are Moniteau County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Statements go out in early November, every bill is due on receipt, and unpaid taxes become delinquent after December 31. If your statement has not arrived by the end of November, the collector asks you to call right away. Failing to receive a statement does not cancel the tax or any penalty and interest.

The assessor's instructions say everyone living in Moniteau County on January 1 should list personal property, including cars, boats and equipment, and that mobile homes must be listed if owned on land belonging to someone else. Household goods, inventories, clothing and personal items are exempt. A couple going through a divorce should note that the collector cannot divide a tax statement later.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Moniteau County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor, then the county Board of Equalization, then the State Tax Commission. The State Tax Commission says appeals to the county board must be filed by the second Monday in July. After a board decision, an owner has thirty days from the date of the decision letter to appeal to the commission, and section 138.430 gives the later of the statutory date or thirty days after the board's final action.

A direct appeal to the commission is allowed in two situations: the assessor did not notify the current owner of a new or increased assessment at least thirty days before the board deadline, or a new owner bought less than thirty days after the county mailed the tax statement. If the property is held by a corporation, LLC, limited partnership, trust or estate, an attorney must file the appeal.

An owner who disputes a value can still pay by December 31 to avoid interest. The commission's guidance says to pay the whole bill to the collector, write "paid under protest" on the check and file a written statement of the grounds with the collector, including the value you believe is right. Taxes paid without protest or an appeal cannot be challenged for that year, though you can appeal the following year's assessment. A buyer who purchases shortly after statements are mailed may also have the direct commission route described above.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Moniteau County homeowners?
sections.html:
The main state program is the Property Tax Credit Claim, often called the circuit breaker. The Missouri Department of Revenue says it gives certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals a credit for part of the real estate tax or rent paid, up to $1,100 for owners who owned and occupied their home and up to $750 for renters. The credit depends on the tax or rent paid and total household income.

A separate exemption exists for former prisoners of war with a total service-connected disability, who own and occupy the property as their homestead. The State Tax Commission lists the proof the assessor will want: evidence of occupancy, a letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs on the disability and a DD 214 or records letter showing POW status.

Active-duty military members stationed away from home under orders are not charged interest on late payment, though the collection fee can still apply, according to the commission's FAQ. Ask the assessor or collector about any local program before you rely on one.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell a Moniteau County house?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for the current balance, including any penalty and interest, before you sign a purchase contract. Delinquent land is subject to sale on the fourth Monday in August under section 140.150, but the owner can pay the taxes, penalty, interest and costs to the collector at any time before the sale. The collector must first mail a notice to the recorded owner by first class mail, and a second certified notice goes out when the assessed value is above $1,000.

Ask whoever handles your closing to settle the balance with the collector's office. Our Missouri property tax guide covers the appeals process statewide, and the Missouri homestead page explains exemptions. The collector posts the current levy sheet on its website for anyone who wants to estimate a bill.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Moniteau County?
faqs.a: The Moniteau County Collector of Revenue, at 200 E. Main Street, Room 101 in California, prepares and mails the statements. The assessor, in Room 105, sets the values the bills are based on.

faqs.q: When does Moniteau County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: All statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. Delinquent land is subject to the collector's tax sale, held on the fourth Monday in August under section 140.150.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Moniteau County assessment?
faqs.a: Appeal to the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. After the board's decision letter, you have thirty days to appeal to the State Tax Commission.

faqs.q: How much of my home's value is taxed in Moniteau County?
faqs.a: Missouri assesses subclass 1 real property at 19 percent of true value, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent under section 137.115. Ask the assessor which subclass your parcel is in.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax relief in Moniteau County?
faqs.a: Seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals may claim the Missouri Property Tax Credit, up to $1,100 for homeowners. Former prisoners of war with a total service-connected disability may qualify for a homestead exemption.
